---
title: "Sensitivity to costs, weights and grade restrictions"
subtitle: "4.10 · settings and sensitivity after the postrank vignette a7"
description: "How withholding costs, criterion weights and grade caps change a report."
---

Changing the withholding cost or the criterion weights changes how the report is evaluated. Changing the
grade cap changes which reports may be chosen.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** Best report states 9 of 15 pairs with wrong shares .0177 and .0267 on scores A and B.
- **A higher price.** States 11 pairs; score B’s wrong share rises to .115 as less certain directions enter.
- **A still higher price.** States 12 pairs while score B’s wrong share falls to .0575; disclosure never falls along this fixed-family path, though individual error shares can move either way.
- **At most two grades.** Best report states 8 pairs with risk .0939; raising the cap can only keep or lower the minimum risk.
- **Thirty-site archive.** Recorded disclosures include 131, 276, 305 and 312 pairs at saved prices without locating continuous transitions.
- **Tutorial archive.** Compares 7 archived settings changing one parameter at a time against the full Cartesian grid in Data.

<details>
<summary>Comparison scope and archive notes</summary>

Along the live path, the withholding cost varies while the posterior, weights and allowed family stay fixed. Each row of the live grid reevaluates the fixed reference report under that row’s loss, even when the cap rules it out of the search. The thirty-site archives use joint posterior draws and show the original solver status and gap. The R example reads the tutorial archive, which varies one setting at a time.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
s <- readRDS(system.file("extdata/cached/tutorial_sensitivity.rds", package="postrank", mustWork=TRUE))$value
s$table[, c("setting_id", "risk", "N")]
```
:::
